findings.detail: controlling_process precedes synchronous accepted registration, and the handler cannot serve until :go after that call replies. Therefore a fast handshake/request EOF cannot reach finished accounting before its map insertion. The internal handler sends one finished event and removes its entry. Exceptional handler death before finished leaves accounting incomplete rather than manufacturing peer EOF; the linked fixture teardown still owns cleanup. General abnormal-process recovery is not newly qualified.

New terminal diagnostics retain only three internally selected fields and at most 16 results. Termination emits counts and those categorical results, not request bytes, socket terms, key/certificate material or unexpected application data. The existing request history is unchanged and is not included in the printed summary. Integer counts can grow, but retained terminal-list cardinality is bounded.

Exactly four ordinary ExUnit controls have no skip tags: silent stall then peer EOF within 250 by 10ms polls; accepted pre-handshake TCP abort; fixture timeout with closed zero; unexpected data with closed zero and no payload in terminal diagnostics. Only the timeout-negative control uses 400 polls to observe the unchanged three-second fixture timeout. Client sockets have after cleanup and fixture children are supervised. Tests are discoverable at the proposed canonical path, and the ordinary host runner uses trace output, formatting and warnings-as-errors compilation. No Elixir parse, format, compile, OTP handshake or scheduling behavior was executed by this review.
